attributes.name: Donna Hope Korzick
attributes.title: Professor
attributes.bio: My research career has been dedicated to various aspects of cardiovascular aging for nearly 20 years and for more than 10 years, a singular focus on mechanistic studies in the aged female heart.  My career in aging research began while a post-doctoral fellow at the NIA (mentor, E. Lakatta) and I have directed my own lab since 2000. My clinical cardiology beginnings (cardiac rehabilitation) provide a clinical perspective to my work, and is the lens through which my hypotheses are derived.
attributes.teaching_interests: Advanced Cellular and Integrative Cardiovascular Physiology, Exercise Physiology
attributes.research_interests: Mitochondrial mechanisms by which aging and estrogen deficiency increase vulnerability to cardiac ischemia-reperfusion injury in the female rat heart, and interventions which confer cardioprotection; role of estrogen receptor signaling and mitochondrial-dependent cell death mechanisms using physiological, biochemical, molecular, and proteomic approaches; mitochondrial respiratory activity and mitochondrial dynamics.
